title: Everyday wonders
author: Astra (Codex / GPT-6; Astra variant unverified)
status: Family pilot staging under /games/; content still for Opus review

cards.title: Right triangles
cards.subject: math
cards.rule: a² + b² = c², where c is the longest side.
cards.example: A 3-by-4 right triangle has a longest side of 5.

cards.title: Percent
cards.subject: math
cards.condition: A percentage change is calculated from its stated starting amount.

cards.title: Force and acceleration
cards.subject: physics
cards.example: A net force of 6 N on 2 kg gives 3 m/s².
cards.condition: Use the combined force on the object, with constant mass.

cards.title: Kinetic energy
cards.subject: physics
cards.rule: Energy of motion = ½ × mass × speed².
cards.example: At the same mass, twice the speed means four times the kinetic energy.
cards.condition: This formula describes ordinary speeds, far below the speed of light.

cards.title: Ohm’s law
cards.subject: physics
cards.condition: Use an ohmic resistor under unchanged physical conditions, including temperature.

cards.title: Density
cards.subject: physics
cards.example: 20 g in 10 cm³ has a density of 2 g/cm³.
cards.condition: For floating, compare the whole object’s average density with the fluid; ignore surface tension here.

cards.title: Oxygen
cards.subject: chemistry
cards.rule: Oxygen atoms have 8 protons; oxygen gas is usually O₂.
cards.example: One O₂ molecule contains two oxygen atoms.
cards.condition: O is the element symbol; O₂ describes a molecule.

cards.title: Gold
cards.subject: chemistry
cards.rule: Gold has the symbol Au and atomic number 79.
cards.condition: Atomic number counts protons, not the total particles in the atom.

cards.title: DNA pairs
cards.subject: biology
cards.rule: In ordinary double-stranded DNA, A pairs with T and C pairs with G.
cards.example: A pairs with T across the two strands.
cards.condition: Pair aligned bases across strands; sequence direction matters when writing whole sequences.

cards.title: Photosynthesis
cards.subject: biology
cards.rule: Plants use light energy to build sugars from carbon dioxide and water, releasing oxygen.
cards.example: The carbon in a plant’s sugars comes from carbon dioxide.
cards.condition: Plants also need minerals and respire; sunlight supplies energy rather than carbon atoms.

cards.title: Average speed
cards.subject: physics
cards.rule: Average speed = total distance ÷ elapsed time.
cards.example: 12 metres in 4 seconds gives an average speed of 3 m/s.
cards.condition: Average speed does not tell you the speed at every instant.

cards.title: Friction
cards.subject: physics
cards.rule: Contact friction resists surfaces sliding, or tending to slide, relative to each other.
cards.example: A shoe can grip the floor because of static friction.
cards.condition: Friction can help you move forward; it does not always act opposite an object’s motion.

rounds.title: Ice in a glass
rounds.prompt: Ice has density 0.92 g/cm³; water has density 1.00 g/cm³. With no trapped air and ignoring surface tension, what happens to the ice?
rounds.discussion: Why can a large hollow metal boat float?

rounds.title: The short sprint
rounds.prompt: A runner covers 20 metres in 5 seconds. What is their average speed?
rounds.discussion: Could the runner have been faster than 4 m/s for part of the run?

rounds.title: DNA partner
rounds.prompt: Which DNA base normally pairs with A in double-stranded DNA?

rounds.title: Pocket-money discount
rounds.prompt: A game costs 80 coins. It is reduced by 25%. What is the new price?
rounds.discussion: Is a 25% increase after this discount enough to return to 80?

rounds.title: Where trees get carbon
rounds.prompt: Where do the carbon atoms in sugars made by a green plant during photosynthesis come from?
rounds.discussion: Why is sunlight essential even though it supplies no carbon atoms?

rounds.title: Shoes that grip
rounds.prompt: When you walk without slipping, what contact force lets the floor push your shoe forward?
rounds.discussion: Why is it harder to walk on a slippery floor?

rounds.title: The ladder puzzle
rounds.prompt: A 5 m ladder rests against a vertical wall on level ground. Its foot is 3 m from the wall. How high up the wall does it reach?
rounds.discussion: Which side of this triangle is the longest?

rounds.title: Gold’s identity
rounds.prompt: What does gold’s atomic number, 79, tell you about every gold atom?

options.text: It has a mass of 79 grams

rounds.discussion: Would an atom with 78 protons still be gold?

rounds.title: Push the trolley
rounds.prompt: A 2 kg trolley has a horizontal net force of 6 N acting on it. What is its acceleration?
rounds.discussion: What if the same net force acts on twice the mass?

rounds.title: Twice as fast
rounds.prompt: The same ball moves at twice its original speed. How does its kinetic energy change?

options.text: It becomes four times as large

rounds.discussion: Why can a modest increase in speed make a big difference?

rounds.title: A small circuit
rounds.prompt: A 9 V source is connected across a 30 Ω ohmic resistor. Resistance stays constant. What current flows?
rounds.discussion: At the same voltage, what happens if resistance doubles?

rounds.title: Reading O₂
rounds.prompt: How many oxygen atoms are in one O₂ molecule?
rounds.discussion: How is the 2 in O₂ different from oxygen’s atomic number 8?
